findings.claim: Both the agent.py comment and docs/analysis.md §8a-2 assert the remove/erase/wipe/clear delete-synonym gap is 'declared open in docs/support-matrix.md', but no such row exists in that file.
findings.evidence: src/browser/agent.py:64 ('declared open in docs/support-matrix.md'); docs/analysis.md:775 ('declared gap in docs/support-matrix.md rather than a guessed-at fix'). grep -n 'remove|erase|wipe|clear|synonym' docs/support-matrix.md returns nothing relevant — the only delete-related row (line 126) is about the verifier, not SCOPE_BLOCK. support-matrix-cites-real-cases only validates that cited case IDs resolve, not that a claimed prose declaration corresponds to a real row, so this is unguarded by any eval.
findings.repro: grep -n 'remove\|erase\|wipe\|clear' docs/support-matrix.md — no hits pertaining to SCOPE_BLOCK's undeleted synonyms.
findings.acceptance: docs/support-matrix.md contains an actual row (or the existing text is corrected) declaring the remove/erase/wipe/clear gap, so the claim in agent.py and analysis.md points to real evidence.
findings.orchestrator_note: Confirmed independently. Two documents of record cite a declaration that does not exist. Dishonest published claim -> blocks.

findings.claim: The superlative/aggregate guard in verifier.py converts a legitimately answerable question into a false FAIL when the page already shows the superlative directly, with no eval case testing this false-positive direction — unlike the delete-determiner fix, which pins both directions.
findings.evidence: src/browser/verifier.py:297 fires aggregate_needs_comparison on any 'which/what/who ... most/least/...' phrasing when there is no expect.answer/state, regardless of whether the answer was directly and correctly extracted from an element that already states the superlative. evals/adversarial/verifier-aggregate-superlative-fails-loud.json contains exactly one row (the failing shape) with no counterpart exercising an answerable superlative.
findings.repro: verify(extractions=[{'value':'Best Seller Badge Product','page_text':'...is our most popular item...'}], answer='Best Seller Badge Product', task='Which product is labeled as the most popular item on this page?') returns FAIL.
findings.acceptance: Either document this as a stated ceiling (false-refusal cost) the way the delete fix documents its determiner scope, or add a case proving the guard does not fire when ground truth makes the answer verifiable — and reconcile with the repo's stated honesty-points cost for false refusals.
findings.orchestrator_note: Confirmed independently. Fail-closed reasoning is sound; the undeclared false-refusal cost is not. Repo precedent D3 and this PR's own subject both say a declared-but-unguarded gap gets falsified -> blocks on the honesty branch.

findings.claim: The widened SCOPE_BLOCK determiner regex over-refuses informational/hypothetical questions about deletion that use the same verb+determiner adjacency as a real command.
findings.evidence: src/browser/agent.py SCOPE_BLOCK matches 'Can you explain how to delete our test entry?' and 'What happens when I delete all the drafts?' — both informational. The pinned case l5-refuse-delete-determiners tests three informational rows, none combining an interrogative frame with an adjacent determiner.
findings.repro: SCOPE_BLOCK.search('What happens when I delete all the drafts?') -> match.
findings.acceptance: Either accept as consistent with the already-declared over-refusal tradeoff and note it for the delete clause, or add a case.
findings.orchestrator_note: LOW, and in the safe direction — same shape as the already-declared login over-refusal. Debt.

findings.claim: The aggregate-superlative regex misses phrasings that don't use which/what/who alongside the exact keyword list, so the same defect class can recur one step removed from the probe's wording.
findings.evidence: _AGGREGATE requires \b(which|what|who)\b.{0,80}\b(most|least|fewest|highest|lowest|greatest)\b; 'Rank the books by price and give me the top one.' does not match.
findings.repro: _AGGREGATE.search('Rank the books by price and give me the top one.') -> no match.
findings.acceptance: Already disclosed by the ponytail comment in verifier.py; logged for completeness, not blocking.
findings.orchestrator_note: LOW and already acknowledged in-code. Debt — and the honest name for the ceiling this PR ships.
